70736.q: What is the ratio of the volume of a sphere to the volume of the cylinder around it?
70736.e: The cylinder has V = π · r² · 2r = 2πr³, the sphere 4/3 · πr³. The ratio is 2 : 3. Archimedes was so proud of this discovery that it is said to have been shown on his grave.
70736.m: A sphere fills two thirds of the cylinder around it.

70737.q: The Earth is approximated as a sphere with a mean radius of 6371 km. Roughly what is its surface area?
70737.e: S = 4 · π · 6371² ≈ 510 million km². About 71 % of it is covered by water.
70737.m: The Earth's surface is about half a billion square kilometres.

70738.q: By what factor must you increase the radius of a sphere to double its volume?
70738.e: The volume grows with r³. For double the volume you need the factor ∛2 ≈ 1.26.
70738.m: To double the volume of a sphere, a radius just over a quarter bigger is enough.

70739.q: What is the volume of a hemisphere with a radius of 6 cm?
70739.m: A hemisphere has a volume of two thirds pi times radius cubed.

70740.q: Along which line does the shortest route between two points on the surface of a sphere run?
a: along a straight line through the North Pole
70740.e: The shortest route on a sphere lies on a great circle, whose centre is the centre of the sphere. That is why long-haul flights often fly seemingly curved routes.
70740.m: The shortest routes on a sphere lie on great circles.

70741.q: What fraction of a cube's volume does a sphere that fits exactly inside it fill?
70741.e: With edge length a, r = a/2. V(sphere) : V(cube) = 4/3 · π · (a/2)³ : a³ = π/6 ≈ 0.524.
70741.m: A sphere inside a cube fills just over half of it.

70742.q: Which information does NOT fix a triangle up to congruence?
a: two sides and the angle between them
one side and the two angles next to it
70742.e: Three angles only fix the shape, not the size. You can enlarge or shrink such a triangle as much as you like.
70742.m: Equal angles alone do not fix the size of a triangle.

70743.q: What does it mean when two shapes are congruent?
a: They are identical in shape and size.
They only have the same shape.
70743.e: Congruent shapes match in shape and size. You can lay one exactly on top of the other.

70744.q: Which information does the congruence rule SAS use?
a: two sides and the angle between them
70744.e: SAS means side, angle, side. The angle must lie between the two given sides.
70744.m: In the SAS congruence rule, the angle lies between the two sides.

70745.q: Under which condition is SSA a valid congruence rule?
a: The angle is opposite the longer side.
The angle is opposite the shorter side.
The sides are the same length.
70745.e: If the given angle is opposite the longer side, there is only one triangle. If it is opposite the shorter side, there can be two different triangles.
70745.m: For SSA, the angle must be opposite the longer side.

70746.q: Can a triangle be constructed from the side lengths 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm?
a: No, because of the triangle inequality.
70746.e: The sum of two sides must be greater than the third. Here 3 + 4 = 7 is less than 8, so there is no triangle.
70746.m: In every triangle, any two sides together are longer than the third.

70747.q: Which transformation is NOT a congruence transformation?
70747.e: Congruence transformations keep lengths and angles. An enlargement with k = 2 doubles all lengths and only produces similar shapes.
70747.m: Translation, rotation and reflection keep the shape and size of a figure.

70748.q: Which information does the congruence rule ASA use?
a: one side and the two angles next to it
one side and an opposite angle
70748.e: ASA means angle, side, angle. The given side lies between the two angles.
70748.m: In the ASA congruence rule, the side lies between the two angles.

70749.q: Why are triangles mainly used in the frameworks of bridges and cranes?
a: Three side lengths fix a triangle uniquely.
70749.e: By the SSS congruence rule, three sides fix a triangle uniquely. So a triangle made of rigid bars cannot change shape, but a quadrilateral can.
70749.m: A triangle made of rigid bars keeps its shape.

70750.m: You calculate the magnitude of a vector with Pythagoras in three dimensions.

70751.q: What is the dot product of (1 | 2 | 3) and (4 | -5 | 6)?
70751.e: You multiply component by component and add: 1·4 + 2·(-5) + 3·6 = 4 − 10 + 18 = 12.
70751.m: The dot product is the sum of the products of the components.

70752.q: How can you tell that two vectors (not the zero vector) are perpendicular?
a: Their sum is the zero vector.
70752.e: a · b = |a| · |b| · cos(φ). At 90°, cos(φ) = 0, so the dot product is zero.
70752.m: Perpendicular vectors have a dot product of zero.

70753.q: Which vector leads from point A(1 | 2) to point B(4 | -2)?
70753.e: The connecting vector is B minus A: (4 − 1 | -2 − 2) = (3 | -4).
70753.m: You get the vector from A to B as end point minus starting point.

70754.q: What is the midpoint of the line segment from A(2 | 4) to B(6 | -2)?
70754.e: The midpoint is the average of the coordinates: ((2 + 6) : 2 | (4 − 2) : 2) = (4 | 1).
70754.m: The midpoint of a line segment has the averages of the coordinates.

70755.q: How is the cross product a × b positioned relative to the vectors a and b?
a: It is parallel to a + b.
70755.e: The cross product of two vectors in space is perpendicular to both. Its magnitude is the area of the parallelogram they span.
70755.m: The cross product gives a normal vector to two vectors.

70756.q: What angle is there between the vectors (1 | 0) and (1 | 1)?
70756.m: You calculate the angle between vectors as the dot product divided by the magnitudes.

70757.q: Which vector is collinear (parallel) to the vector (2 | -4)?
70757.e: (-3 | 6) = -1.5 · (2 | -4). Collinear vectors are multiples of each other.
70757.m: Two vectors are collinear if one is a multiple of the other.

70758.q: Two forces of 30 N and 40 N act at right angles to each other on the same point. How big is the resulting force?
70758.e: Forces are added as vectors. At 90°, √(30² + 40²) = √2500 = 50 N.
70758.m: Forces are added like vectors, not simply like numbers.

70759.q: What are the coordinates of the point on the unit circle that belongs to the angle α?
70759.e: In the unit circle with radius 1, the x-coordinate is the adjacent side and the y-coordinate the opposite side. So x = cos α and y = sin α.
70759.m: On the unit circle, the x-coordinate is the cosine and the y-coordinate is the sine.

70760.q: What is the value of cos(180°)?
70760.e: On the unit circle, 180° belongs to the point (-1 | 0). The x-coordinate is -1.
70760.m: At 180 degrees, the point is on the left edge of the unit circle.

70761.q: In which range is the sine positive and the cosine negative?
70761.e: Between 90° and 180° the point is in the 2nd quadrant: on the left (x negative) and at the top (y positive).
70761.m: In the second quadrant the sine is positive and the cosine negative.

70762.q: Which value is equal to sin(120°)?
70762.e: sin(180° − α) = sin(α). So sin(120°) = sin(60°).
70762.m: Supplementary angles have the same sine.

70763.q: What symmetry does the cosine function have because cos(-α) = cos(α)?
70763.e: On the unit circle, -α is reflected in the x-axis and the x-coordinate stays the same. So the graph of the cosine is symmetrical about the y-axis.
70763.m: The cosine is an even function.

70764.q: Roughly how many degrees is 1 radian, the angle with an arc length of 1 on the unit circle?
70764.e: A full circle is 2π rad = 360°. So 1 rad = 180° : π ≈ 57.3°.
70764.m: A radian is the angle whose arc on the unit circle has length one.

70765.q: What is the value of sin(3π/2)?
70765.e: 3π/2 corresponds to 270°. The matching point on the unit circle is (0 | -1), so sin = -1.
70765.m: At 270 degrees, the point is at the bottom of the unit circle.

70766.q: For which angle is tan(α) not defined?
70766.e: tan(α) = sin(α) : cos(α). At 90°, cos(α) = 0, and you must not divide by zero.
70766.m: The tangent is not defined where the cosine is zero.

70767.q: What is the period of the sine function in radians?
70767.e: After one full turn of 360° = 2π on the unit circle, all values repeat.
70767.m: Sine and cosine repeat after one full turn.

70768.q: What is the exact value of sin(225°)?
70768.e: 225° = 180° + 45° is in the 3rd quadrant, where the sine is negative. So sin(225°) = -sin(45°) = -√2 / 2.
70768.m: In the third quadrant, sine and cosine are both negative.

70769.q: When you roll a fair dice, what is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
70769.e: The favourable numbers are 5 and 6, so 2 of 6 equally likely outcomes. 2/6 simplified is 1/3.
70769.m: In a Laplace experiment you divide the number of favourable outcomes by the number of possible outcomes.

70770.q: When rolling two fair dice, what is the probability of a total of 7?
70770.e: The total 7 comes from 6 of the 36 equally likely pairs (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). 6/36 gives 1/6.
70770.m: With two dice, 7 is the most common total.

70771.q: When rolling two fair dice, what is the probability of a total of 2?
70771.e: The total 2 only comes from the pair (1,1). That is 1 of 36 equally likely outcomes.
70771.m: With two dice there are 36 equally likely pairs.

70772.q: Which condition must a random experiment meet to be a Laplace experiment?
70772.e: A Laplace experiment has finitely many outcomes that all have the same probability. Only then does the formula favourable over possible outcomes apply.
70772.m: The Laplace formula only applies if all outcomes are equally likely.

70773.q: One card is drawn at random from a 36-card Jass deck. What is the probability of an ace?
70773.e: A Jass deck has four suits with one ace each, so 4 aces. 4/36 simplified gives 1/9.
70773.m: When drawing from a well-shuffled deck, every card is equally likely.

70774.q: A bag holds 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green balls. What is the probability of not drawing a blue ball?
70774.e: 3 + 2, so 5 of the 10 balls, are not blue. 5/10 is 1/2.
70774.m: Instead of counting the favourable cases, you can also look at the opposite event.

70775.q: A fair coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting tails at least once?
70775.e: The opposite event is “three heads” with probability 1/8. So 1 − 1/8, which gives 7/8.
70775.m: For “at least once” it is often easiest to use the opposite event.

70776.q: Someone guesses a four-digit PIN with the digits 0 to 9 at random. What is the probability of getting it right first time?
70776.e: There are 10 digits for each of the 4 places, so 10 to the power of 4 equals 10000 codes. Only one of them is right.
70776.m: The number of codes grows by a factor of ten with each extra digit.

70777.q: According to the first path rule, what do you do with the probabilities along a path in a tree diagram?
70777.e: By the path multiplication rule, the probability of a path is the product of all the probabilities along that path.
70777.m: Along a path, the probabilities are multiplied.

70778.q: According to the second path rule, what do you do with the probabilities of several paths belonging to the same event?
70778.e: By the path addition rule, the probability of an event is the sum of the probabilities of all its paths.
70778.m: The probabilities of different paths to the same event are added.

70779.q: What do the probabilities of all the branches from one node of a tree diagram add up to?
70779.e: From a node, exactly one of the possible cases is certain to happen. So the branch probabilities add up to 1.
70779.m: At every branching point, the probabilities add up to one.

70780.q: An urn holds 4 red and 6 blue balls. You draw twice without replacement. What is the probability of two red balls?
70780.e: On the first draw P(red) is 4/10, on the second only 3/9. The product 4/10 · 3/9 gives 12/90, so 2/15.
70780.m: Without replacement, the probabilities change from stage to stage.

70781.q: An urn holds 4 red and 6 blue balls. You draw twice with replacement. What is the probability of two red balls?
70781.e: With replacement, P(red) stays 0.4 on every draw. The product 0.4 · 0.4 gives 0.16.
70781.m: With replacement, the probabilities stay the same at every stage.

70782.q: A fair die is rolled twice. What is the probability of at least one six?
70782.e: No six has the probability 5/6 · 5/6 equals 25/36. At least one six is the opposite event: 1 − 25/36 gives 11/36.
70782.m: Using the opposite probability often saves drawing many paths in a tree diagram.

70783.q: How many paths does the complete tree diagram for tossing a coin three times have?
70783.e: Each stage doubles the number of paths: 2 · 2 · 2 gives 8.
70783.m: In multi-stage experiments, you multiply the number of options at each stage.

70784.q: A bus is late with a probability of 20 %. If it is late, Lea is late for school with a probability of 50 %, otherwise 5 %. What is the probability that she is late?
70784.e: The two paths give 0.2 · 0.5 equals 0.10 and 0.8 · 0.05 equals 0.04. Together that is 0.14, so 14 %.
70784.m: You get the total probability as the sum of all matching paths.

70785.q: What is the value of 5! (5 factorial)?
70785.m: The factorial of a number is the product of all natural numbers from one up to that number.

70786.q: What is the value of 0! by definition?
70786.e: 0! is defined as 1, because there is exactly one way to arrange zero objects. This also makes formulas like n! equals n · (n − 1)! work for n equal to 1.
70786.m: Zero factorial is defined as one.

70787.q: What is the value of the fraction 10! / 8!?
70787.e: Almost all the factors cancel: 10! / 8! gives 10 · 9, so 90.
70787.m: With quotients of factorials, you cancel the common factors.

70788.q: In how many ways can 6 people stand in a row?
70788.e: There are 6 options for the first place, then 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. That gives 6! equals 720.
70788.m: The number of arrangements of n different objects is n factorial.

70789.q: How many zeros does the number 10! end with?
70789.e: 10! is 3628800. The zeros come from pairs of factors 2 · 5, and 10! contains the factor 5 exactly twice (in 5 and 10).
70789.m: You count the trailing zeros of a factorial by counting the factors of five it contains.

70790.q: From which natural number n is n! greater than 2ⁿ for the first time?
70790.e: For n = 3, 3! = 6 < 8 = 2³. For n = 4, 4! = 24 > 16 = 2⁴, and from then on the factorial grows faster.
70790.m: In the long run, the factorial grows faster than any power of two.

70791.q: How many different sequences of letters can be made from the letters of the word “AARAU”?
70791.e: There are 5! arrangements, but the three As are identical. So you divide by 3!: 120 / 6 gives 20.
70791.m: With identical elements, you divide by the factorial of how many there are.

70792.q: What is the value of the fraction 100! / 99!?
70792.e: 100! equals 100 · 99!. So the fraction gives exactly 100.
70792.m: Every factorial is the number itself times the factorial of the number before it.

70793.q: What is the value of the binomial coefficient “5 choose 2”?
70793.m: The binomial coefficient “n choose k” counts the ways of choosing k out of n elements without order.

70794.q: How many subsets (including the empty set) does a set with 5 elements have?
70794.e: The sum of all binomial coefficients “5 choose k” for k from 0 to 5 is 1 + 5 + 10 + 10 + 5 + 1, so 32. That is 2 to the power of 5.
70794.m: The sum of a row in Pascal's triangle is a power of two.

70795.q: What is the value of the binomial coefficient “12 choose 11”?
70795.e: Because of symmetry, “12 choose 11” equals “12 choose 1”, which is 12.
70795.m: The binomial coefficient “n choose k” equals “n choose n minus k”.

70796.q: What is the value of “n choose 0” for every natural number n?
70796.e: There is exactly one way to choose none out of n elements, namely the empty choice.
70796.m: There is exactly one way to choose zero elements.

70797.q: In how many ways can you form a team of 2 and a team of 4 from 6 people?
70797.e: Once you choose the 2 people, the team of 4 is fixed. “6 choose 2” gives 6 · 5 / 2, so 15.
70797.m: If you choose k out of n elements, the rest is automatically determined.

70798.q: In which arrangement of numbers do the binomial coefficients appear row by row?
70798.e: In Pascal's triangle each number is the sum of the two numbers above it. Row n contains exactly the binomial coefficients “n choose k”.
70798.m: In Pascal's triangle, each number is the sum of the two numbers above it.

70799.q: A committee of 3 is chosen from 8 pupils. How many possibilities are there?
70799.m: For a choice without order, you divide by the factorial of the size of the choice.

70800.q: What is the coefficient of the term x²y⁴ when (x + y)⁶ is expanded?
70800.e: By the binomial theorem, the coefficient is “6 choose 2”, so 6 · 5 / 2 equals 15.
70800.m: The binomial theorem gives the coefficients as binomial coefficients.

70801.q: A fair die is rolled four times. What is the probability of exactly two sixes (rounded)?
70801.e: By the binomial distribution: “4 choose 2” · (1/6)² · (5/6)², so 6 · 25 / 1296 equals 150 / 1296, about 0.116.
70801.m: In the binomial distribution, the binomial coefficient counts the possible orders of the successes.

70802.q: A wheel of fortune pays nothing with probability 1/2, three francs with 1/3 and twelve francs with 1/6. What is the expected payout?
70802.e: You weight each payout by its probability: 0 · 1/2 + 3 · 1/3 + 12 · 1/6 gives 0 + 1 + 2, so 3 francs.
70802.m: The expected value is the sum of the values times their probabilities.

70803.q: A lottery ticket costs 2 francs. With probability 1/10 you win 15 francs, otherwise nothing. What is the expected profit per ticket?
70803.e: The expected payout is 15 · 1/10 equals 1.50 francs. Minus the 2 franc stake, that leaves -0.50 francs.
70803.m: The expected profit is the expected payout minus the stake.

70804.q: What is the expected value of the profit in a fair game?
70804.e: A game is called fair if, in the long run, neither the player nor the organiser wins. So the expected profit is zero.
70804.m: In a fair game, the expected profit is zero.

70805.q: A fair die is rolled 60 times. How many sixes do you expect?
70805.e: For the binomial distribution the expected value is n · p, so 60 · 1/6 equals 10.
70805.m: With n independent trials and a success probability p, you expect n times p successes.

70806.q: What is the expected value of the total when rolling two fair dice?
70806.e: Expected values can be added: 3.5 + 3.5 gives 7.
70806.m: The expected value of a sum is the sum of the expected values.

70807.q: In roulette with 37 numbers, you bet 1 franc on red (18 red numbers) and get 2 francs back if you win. What is the expected profit?
70807.e: You win 1 franc with 18/37 and lose 1 franc with 19/37. The expected value is 18/37 − 19/37 equals -1/37 francs, about -2.7 centimes.
70807.m: Because of the green zero, the casino has an advantage in roulette.

70808.q: A random variable X has the expected value 4. What is the expected value of 2X + 3?
70808.e: The expected value is linear: 2 · 4 + 3 gives 11.
70808.m: Linear changes to a random variable have the same effect on its expected value.

70809.q: Damage worth 20,000 francs occurs with a probability of 0.5 % per year. What is the expected damage per year?
70809.e: You calculate 20,000 · 0.005, which gives 100 francs. Insurers calculate premiums starting from such expected values.
70809.m: Insurance premiums are based on the expected damage plus costs.

70810.q: Which law says that the average of many repetitions approaches the expected value?
70810.e: The law of large numbers says that with many independent repetitions, the average approaches the expected value.
70810.m: The more often you repeat an experiment, the closer the average gets to the expected value.

70811.q: What does the standard deviation of a data set describe?
a: How widely the values are spread around the mean
Where the middle of the values is
70811.e: The standard deviation is a measure of spread. A small standard deviation means the values are close to the mean.
70811.m: The larger the standard deviation, the more widely the values are spread.

70812.q: How are standard deviation and variance related?
a: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance
The variance is half the standard deviation
They are always the same size
The variance is the square root of the standard deviation
70812.e: The variance is the mean of the squared deviations. Taking its square root gives the standard deviation.
70812.m: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

70813.q: 10 is added to every value in a data set. What happens to the standard deviation?
70813.e: All the values and the mean move by 10. The distances from the mean stay the same, and so does the spread.
70813.m: Shifting all the values does not change the spread.

70814.q: Every value in a data set is doubled. What happens to the standard deviation?
70814.e: All the distances from the mean double, and so does the standard deviation. The variance, however, quadruples.
70814.m: If each value is multiplied by a factor, the standard deviation is multiplied by the same factor.

70815.q: A fair coin is tossed 100 times. What is the standard deviation of the number of heads?
70815.e: For the binomial distribution, σ equals the square root of n · p · (1 − p). With 100 · 0.5 · 0.5 equals 25, the square root is 5.
70815.m: The standard deviation of the binomial distribution is the square root of n times p times one minus p.

70816.q: What is the standard deviation of the data set 5, 5, 5, 5?
70816.e: All the values equal the mean 5, so there are no deviations. That is why the standard deviation is 0.
70816.m: If all the values are the same, there is no spread.

70817.q: What unit does the standard deviation of heights measured in centimetres have?
70817.e: The variance has the unit square centimetres. Taking the square root gives the standard deviation the same unit as the data again.
70817.m: The standard deviation has the same unit as the measured values.

70818.q: What is the standard deviation of the two values 10 and 20 (as a population)?
70818.e: The mean is 15, and both values differ from it by 5. The variance is (25 + 25) / 2 equals 25, and the square root is 5.
70818.m: For two values, the population standard deviation is half the distance between them.

70819.q: Roughly what proportion of the values of a normal distribution lies within the mean plus or minus one standard deviation?
70819.e: In a normal distribution, about 68.3 % of the values lie within one standard deviation of the mean.
70819.m: About two thirds of the values lie within one standard deviation of the mean.

70820.q: Roughly what proportion of the values of a normal distribution lies within the mean plus or minus two standard deviations?
70820.e: About 95.4 % of the values lie within two standard deviations of the mean.
70820.m: Almost all values, about 95 per cent, lie within two standard deviations.

70821.q: Roughly what proportion of the values of a normal distribution lies within the mean plus or minus three standard deviations?
70821.e: About 99.7 % of the values lie within three standard deviations of the mean.
70821.m: Values beyond three standard deviations are very rare in a normal distribution.

70822.q: After which mathematician is the bell curve of the normal distribution often named?
70822.e: The density curve is also called the Gaussian bell curve. Carl Friedrich Gauss used the distribution, among other things, to describe measurement errors.
70822.m: After Carl Friedrich Gauss, the normal distribution is also called the Gaussian distribution.

70823.q: IQ scores are normally distributed with mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Roughly what proportion has an IQ above 115?
70823.e: 115 is one standard deviation above the mean. About 68 % lie within plus or minus 1σ, which leaves about 16 % on each side.
70823.m: About sixteen per cent of the values lie more than one standard deviation above the mean.

70824.q: What mean and standard deviation does the standard normal distribution have?
70824.e: The standard normal distribution has mean μ equal to 0 and standard deviation σ equal to 1. Any normal distribution can be converted to it.
70824.m: The standard normal distribution has mean zero and standard deviation one.

70825.q: Heights are normally distributed with mean 170 cm and standard deviation 8 cm. What is the z-score of a height of 180 cm?
70825.m: The z-score tells you how many standard deviations a value is from the mean.

70826.q: Where are the points of inflection of the bell curve of a normal distribution?
a: At the mean plus or minus one standard deviation
At plus or minus two standard deviations
70826.e: The bell curve changes the way it curves exactly one standard deviation to the left and right of the mean.
70826.m: The points of inflection of the bell curve are one standard deviation from the mean.

70827.q: In which range does Pearson's correlation coefficient lie?
70827.e: The correlation coefficient r can take values from -1 to 1. The closer its absolute value is to 1, the stronger the linear relationship.
70827.m: The correlation coefficient always lies between minus one and one.

70828.q: What does a correlation coefficient of r equal to -1 mean?
70828.e: With r equal to -1, all the points lie exactly on a downward-sloping line: the larger x, the smaller y.
70828.m: A correlation coefficient of minus one means a perfect falling linear relationship.

70829.q: What does a correlation coefficient of r equal to 0 mean?
70829.e: r equal to 0 means there is no linear relationship. A non-linear relationship, such as a parabola, is still possible.
70829.m: A correlation coefficient of zero only rules out a linear relationship.

70830.q: Ice cream sales and the number of swimming accidents are positively correlated. What is the most likely explanation?
a: A third variable such as warm weather
Swimming accidents boost ice cream sales
70830.e: Both rise in warm weather. The correlation comes from this third variable and is no proof of cause.
70830.m: A correlation does not yet prove a causal link.

70831.q: What is the coefficient of determination r² if the correlation coefficient r is 0.8?
70831.e: You square r: 0.8 · 0.8 gives 0.64. So about 64 % of the spread is explained by the linear relationship.
70831.m: In linear regression, the coefficient of determination is the square of the correlation coefficient.

70832.q: After which statistician is the usual correlation coefficient for linear relationships named?
70832.e: The product-moment correlation coefficient is named after the British statistician Karl Pearson.
70832.m: The correlation coefficient for linear relationships is called Pearson correlation.

70833.q: Which correlation coefficient is typically used for ranked data, such as league tables?
70833.e: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient compares the ranks instead of the measured values themselves. It also captures monotonic, non-linear relationships.
70833.m: For rankings, you use Spearman's rank correlation.

70834.q: Which method is usually used to find the regression line through a scatter plot?
70834.e: The regression line is placed so that the sum of the squared vertical distances from the points to the line is as small as possible.
70834.m: The regression line minimises the sum of the squared deviations.

70835.q: In roulette, red has come up five times in a row. What is the probability of black on the next spin?
70835.e: The spins are independent; the ball has no memory. Believing black is now “due” is called the gambler's fallacy.
70835.m: Independent random events have no memory.

70836.q: A survey on a sports website finds that 80 % of participants do sport every day. Why can you not apply this to the whole population?
70836.e: Mainly sporty people take part on a sports website. This selection bias makes the sample useless for statements about everyone.
70836.m: Only a representative sample lets you draw conclusions about the whole population.

70837.q: What is the phenomenon called where a trend in all subgroups reverses when the groups are combined?
70837.e: In Simpson's paradox, subgroups show a different trend from the combined data, often because the groups are of different sizes.
70837.m: Combined data can show a different trend from their subgroups.

70838.q: In the Second World War, people wanted to reinforce planes where returning aircraft had bullet holes. What thinking error is in this?
70838.e: They only saw the planes that came back. The statistician Abraham Wald advised reinforcing exactly the places without bullet holes, because hits there led to crashes.
70838.m: If you only look at the survivors, you easily draw wrong conclusions.

70840.q: In the Monty Hall problem you have chosen a door, and the host opens another door with a goat. What is your chance of winning if you switch?
70840.e: The door chosen first only wins with 1/3. Because the host deliberately shows a goat, the remaining probability of 2/3 goes to the other closed door.
70840.m: In the Monty Hall problem, switching doubles your chance of winning.

70841.q: Why is the median often more meaningful than the arithmetic mean for a population's income?
a: The mean is strongly distorted by very high incomes
The mean is hard to calculate
The median weights all values equally
70841.e: A few very high incomes pull the mean upwards. The median divides the population into two equal halves and is robust against outliers.
70841.m: For skewed distributions, the median describes the middle better than the mean.

70842.q: What is it called when an extreme measurement is usually followed by a less extreme one when repeated?
70842.e: Extreme results often contain a large element of chance. When repeated, the result is therefore usually closer to the average, even without any action.
70842.m: Extreme chance results are usually followed by more average ones.

70843.q: A bar chart's y-axis starts at 95 instead of 0. What impression does this create?
70843.e: With the cut-off axis, bars of 96 and 97 look as if one were twice as tall as the other. In reality they differ by only about 1 %.
70843.m: A cut-off y-axis can make small differences look dramatic.

70844.q: How much interest do 5000 francs earn in one year at an interest rate of 2 %?
70844.e: The annual interest is 5000 · 2 / 100, so 100 francs.
70844.m: You calculate annual interest as capital times interest rate divided by a hundred.

70845.q: How much interest do 12,000 francs earn at 1.5 % in 120 days (year of 360 days)?
70845.e: You calculate 12,000 · 1.5 / 100 · 120 / 360. The annual interest of 180 francs is cut to a third, so 60 francs.
70845.m: For interest over part of a year, you multiply the annual interest by the fraction of days.

70846.q: What is the interest for part of an interest period called, for example when buying a bond during the year?
70846.e: Accrued interest (in Switzerland “Marchzins”) is the interest built up since the last interest date. The buyer of a bond pays it to the seller on top of the price.
70846.m: Accrued interest is the interest for part of an interest period.

70847.q: A bank account earns 500 francs of interest per year. How much withholding tax (35 %) does the bank deduct?
70847.e: You calculate 500 · 35 / 100, which gives 175 francs. You can reclaim the withholding tax through your tax return.
70847.m: Withholding tax on interest in Switzerland is thirty-five per cent.

70848.q: Capital earns 90 francs of interest in one year at 3 %. How large is the capital?
70848.e: From interest equals capital times 3 / 100 it follows that capital equals 90 · 100 / 3, so 3000 francs.
70848.m: You get the capital as interest times a hundred divided by the interest rate.

70849.q: 8000 francs earn 240 francs of interest in one year. What is the interest rate?
70849.m: You get the interest rate as interest divided by capital times a hundred.

70850.q: How much interest do 1000 francs earn in 3 years at 4 % simple interest (no compound interest)?
70850.e: The simple annual interest is 40 francs. Over 3 years without interest on the interest, that gives 3 · 40 equals 120 francs.
70850.m: With simple interest, only the starting capital earns interest.

70851.q: How much interest do 6000 francs earn at 2 % in 3 months?
70851.e: The annual interest is 120 francs. Three months are a quarter of the year, so 30 francs.
70851.m: For monthly interest, you divide the annual interest by twelve and multiply by the number of months.

70852.q: What does the effective interest rate of a loan take into account in addition to the nominal rate?
70852.e: The effective rate includes processing fees and how the payments are spread. It shows the real annual cost of the loan.
70852.m: The effective interest rate shows the real cost of a loan.

70853.q: A loan has a nominal rate of 12 % a year, charged monthly at 1 %. Roughly what is the effective rate?
70853.e: You calculate 1.01 to the power of 12 minus 1, which gives about 0.1268. Because the interest is charged on the interest every month, the effective rate is above 12 %.
70853.m: With interest charged several times a year, the effective rate is higher than the nominal rate.

70854.q: You are paid out 4900 francs (a 5000 franc loan minus a 100 franc fee) and pay back 5250 francs after one year. Roughly what is the effective rate?
70854.e: The cost is 5250 − 4900, so 350 francs. Based on the 4900 francs actually received, that gives about 7.14 %.
70854.m: Fees push the effective rate above the nominal rate.

70855.q: What is a constant instalment made up of interest and repayment called?
70855.e: With an annuity loan the instalment stays the same. The interest share falls over time and the repayment share rises.
70855.m: With an annuity, the instalment stays the same while the shares of interest and repayment shift.

70856.q: What is paying back the borrowed capital of a loan called?
70856.e: Repayment, in Switzerland often called amortisation, reduces the remaining debt. The interest is the price for borrowing.
70856.m: With repayment, you pay back the debt itself.

70857.q: What is true of an instalment loan with a constant repayment?
a: The instalments fall from year to year
The instalments always stay the same
The instalments rise from year to year
70857.e: The repayment is the same each year, but the interest is calculated on a falling remaining debt. So the total instalments get smaller.
70857.m: With constant repayment, the interest and therefore the instalments fall.

70858.q: How much equity do Swiss banks usually require at least for buying a home?
70858.e: At least 20 % equity is usual, of which at least 10 % must be so-called “hard” equity that does not come from the pension fund.
70858.m: For a mortgage in Switzerland you usually need at least a fifth of the price as equity.

70859.q: Loan A has a nominal rate of 8 % plus processing fees, loan B has a nominal rate of 9 % with no fees. Which figure must you compare to find the cheaper offer?
70859.e: The nominal rate alone is misleading, because fees increase the cost. The effective rate includes all costs and makes offers comparable.
70859.m: You compare loan offers by their effective interest rate.

70860.q: An interest rate rises from 2 % to 3 %. How do you describe this change correctly?
70860.e: The difference is 1 percentage point. Relative to the old 2 %, that is a relative increase of 50 %.
70860.m: Percentage points describe the absolute difference, per cent the relative change.

70861.q: The unemployment rate rises from 4 % to 5 %. By what percentage has it risen?
70861.e: The increase is 1 percentage point. In relative terms that is 1 / 4, so 25 %.
70861.m: An increase of one percentage point can be much more than one per cent in relative terms.

70862.q: A party increases its share of the vote from 20 % to 25 %. By how many percentage points has it gained?
70862.e: The difference in the shares is 25 − 20, so 5 percentage points. In relative terms that is an increase of 25 %.
70862.m: You give the difference between two percentages in percentage points.

70863.q: In 2024 the standard rate of Swiss VAT rose from 7.7 % to 8.1 %. By how much did it rise?
70863.e: The difference between the rates is 8.1 − 7.7, so 0.4 percentage points. In relative terms that is about 5.2 %.
70863.m: Changes in tax rates are correctly given in percentage points.

70864.q: A share falls from 10 % to 8 %. By what percentage has it fallen?
70864.e: The decrease is 2 percentage points. Relative to the original 10 %, that is 2 / 10, so 20 %.
70864.m: Relative changes always refer to the starting value.

70865.q: A central bank raises its key interest rate by 50 basis points. How many percentage points is that?
70865.e: A basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point. So 50 basis points are 0.5 percentage points.
70865.m: A hundred basis points make one percentage point.

70866.q: An interest rate rises from 3 % to 6 %. By what percentage has it risen?
70866.e: The interest rate has doubled: up 3 percentage points, in relative terms 3 / 3 equals 100 %.
70866.m: Doubling corresponds to an increase of a hundred per cent.

70867.q: Voter turnout rises from 45 % to 48 %. By what percentage has it risen (rounded)?
70867.e: The increase is 3 percentage points. In relative terms that is 3 / 45, about 6.7 %.
70867.m: For the relative increase, you divide the difference by the old value.

a: A group of jobs with similar tasks
A field where apprentices play sport
The list of all open apprenticeships
73031.e: An occupational field groups together jobs that have similar tasks, materials or workplaces. That makes it easier to find related jobs.
73031.m: An occupational field groups related jobs together.

73032.q: Which occupational field does the job of healthcare assistant (FaGe) belong to?
73032.e: Healthcare assistants care for and look after people in hospitals, care homes and home care services. That is why the job belongs to the health field.
73032.m: If you care for people, you work in the health field.

73033.q: Which job belongs to the construction field?
73033.e: Bricklayers build walls and buildings on the building site. That is why their job belongs to the construction field.
73033.m: Bricklayers work in the construction field.

73034.q: Which job fits the IT field?
73034.e: IT specialists develop programs or look after computers and networks. That is typical of the IT field.
73034.m: IT specialists program and look after computer systems.

73035.q: In which occupational field do farmers, gardeners and forest workers work?
73035.e: These jobs have to do with plants, animals, soil and forests. That is why they belong to the nature field.
73035.m: Jobs with plants, animals and forests belong to the nature field.

73036.q: Which job belongs to the hospitality field?
73036.e: Cooks prepare food in restaurants, hotels and canteens. That is part of hospitality.

73037.q: What do logistics workers EFZ mainly do?
73037.e: Logistics workers make sure goods arrive in the right place. They work in warehouses, at the post office or for transport companies.
73037.m: Logistics workers store and distribute goods.

73038.q: Why is it worth looking at a whole occupational field when choosing a career?
a: You discover related jobs you didn't know about
Because otherwise you won't get an apprenticeship
Because all jobs in the field pay the same
Because that is the only way into vocational school
73038.e: If you fix on just one job, you often overlook similar ones. The same field offers alternatives in case your dream job doesn't work out.
73038.m: Looking at the whole field shows you more options.

73039.q: Why is it important to know your own interests when choosing a career?
a: A job that interests you is more likely to be enjoyable
Because interests must be written in the apprenticeship contract
Because otherwise you may not write a CV
73039.e: If you are interested in the tasks of a job, you stay more motivated and learn more easily. That is why getting to know your own interests is a first step in choosing a career.
73039.m: Your interests show you which work you might enjoy.

73040.q: What is an example of a practical, hands-on strength?
a: Speaking well in front of people
73040.e: Hands-on strengths have to do with your hands and with tools. They are important, for example, in jobs such as joiner or mechanic.
73040.m: Practical skill shows in how you handle tools and materials.

73041.q: What is meant by social skills?
a: The ability to get on well with other people
73041.e: Social skills include teamwork, politeness and helpfulness, for example. They are important in almost every job.
73041.m: Social skills mean getting on well with other people.

73042.q: What is a good way to find out where your strengths lie?
a: Only look at how much a job pays
Take the same job as your best friend
Roll a dice and pick a job at random
73042.e: Parents, teachers or friends often see strengths you don't notice yourself. Your own view combined with other people's views gives a good picture.
73042.m: Feedback from others helps you recognise your strengths.

73043.q: Which quality is especially important for a job with lots of customer contact?
73043.e: Anyone who deals with lots of customers, for example in retail, should be friendly and open. That builds trust.
73043.m: With customers, friendliness is especially important.

73044.q: For which job is a head for heights especially important?
73044.e: Roofers work on roofs high up. If you are afraid of heights, you can put yourself and others in danger.
73044.m: If you work high up, you need a head for heights.

73045.q: What is meant by “self-assessment” when choosing a career?
a: You judge your own abilities yourself
A test marked by the training company
The mark from your class teacher
73045.e: In a self-assessment you think about what you are good at and like doing. It is often compared with how others assess you.
73045.m: In a self-assessment you judge yourself.

73046.e: Personal skills are about how you manage yourself, such as punctuality, reliability and determination. Training companies pay close attention to them.
73046.m: Reliability and staying power are important personal skills.

73047.q: What is an important aim of a taster apprenticeship?
a: To check whether the job really suits you
To take the final apprenticeship exam
73047.e: On a taster placement you see everyday working life up close. That way you notice whether the tasks and working environment match what you imagined.
73047.m: On a taster placement you check whether a job suits you.

73048.q: How do you usually get a taster apprenticeship?
a: You win one in a prize draw
You must start the apprenticeship first
73048.e: Young people usually organise taster placements themselves by phone, email or through online platforms. The careers advice service can help too.
73048.m: You usually arrange a taster placement yourself with the company.

73049.q: How should you behave on your first taster day?
a: Arrive on time and ask questions
Be as quiet as possible and ask nothing
Use your phone all the time
73049.e: Being on time and showing interest make a good impression. If you ask questions, you get to know the job better.
73049.m: On a taster placement, be on time and show interest.

73050.q: What do young people often get from the company after a taster apprenticeship?
a: An apprenticeship contract signed by the canton
73050.e: Many companies fill in an assessment form after the taster placement. You can later add good assessments to your application.
73050.m: Good taster reports strengthen your application.

73051.q: Why is it worth writing a taster diary or report after a taster placement?
a: You record what you liked and what you didn't
Because the apprenticeship contract requires it
Because otherwise you won't be paid
Because the report replaces the final mark
73051.e: A report helps you compare impressions and make better decisions later. It is also useful when talking to your parents and the careers adviser.
73051.m: A taster report helps you compare jobs.

73052.q: How long does a taster apprenticeship usually last?
a: A few days to about a week
73052.e: A taster placement usually lasts between one and five days. That is enough to get a good insight.
73052.m: A taster placement usually lasts only a few days.

73053.q: What makes sense if you didn't like a taster apprenticeship at all?
a: Think about what exactly didn't suit you
Give up choosing a career altogether
Never go on a taster placement again
Write the company a nasty message
73053.e: Even a bad experience is valuable, because you learn what you don't want. That way you can search more precisely.
73053.m: Even a disappointing taster placement helps you move on.

73054.q: Why is it good to try out several different jobs on taster placements?
a: You can compare the jobs with each other
Because that is the only way to get an ID card
Because every company pays for it
Because a single taster placement is not allowed
73054.e: If you get to know several jobs, you can compare them better and decide more confidently. You often discover new interests along the way.
73054.m: Several taster placements make it easier to compare jobs.

73055.q: What does the abbreviation BIZ stand for in career choice?
a: Bildungs- und Industriezentrale (education and industry office)
73055.e: At the careers information centre (BIZ) you find information about jobs, training and further education. It is run by the cantonal careers advice service.
73055.m: BIZ is short for careers information centre.

73056.q: Who runs the careers information centres in Switzerland?
73056.e: Careers, study and career-path advice is the cantons' responsibility. The careers information centres belong to these cantonal services.
73056.m: The BIZ belong to the cantonal careers advice service.

73057.q: What does a visit to the information library at the BIZ usually cost young people choosing a career?
73057.e: The information services of the careers information centres are free for young people choosing a career. That way everyone has access to careers information.
73057.m: The BIZ is free for young people choosing a career.

73058.q: What do you typically find at the BIZ?
73058.e: At the BIZ there is information material such as leaflets and films about many jobs. Experts also offer advice sessions.
73058.m: At the BIZ you find information and advice about jobs.

73059.q: Who works at the BIZ and advises young people?
73059.e: Trained careers, study and career-path advisers work at the BIZ. They support young people and adults with questions about training.
73059.m: At the BIZ, careers advice experts help you.

73060.q: What is the best way to prepare for an advice session at the BIZ?
a: Write down your own questions and interests
Bring an apprenticeship contract with you
73060.e: If you write down your questions and interests, you make better use of the session. School reports or taster reports are also helpful.
73060.m: Before the session, write down your questions and interests.

73061.q: Besides young people, who else may use the services of the BIZ?
a: Adults who want further training or a change of direction
73061.e: Careers, study and career-path advice is also there for adults. It helps with further training or changing jobs, for example.
73061.m: Adults can also get advice at the BIZ.

a: The official website of Swiss careers advice
A site only for university students
The website of a single company
73062.e: berufsberatung.ch is the official website of careers, study and career-path advice. There you find job descriptions, apprenticeships and tips for applying.
73062.m: berufsberatung.ch is the official website of Swiss careers advice.

73063.q: What is the apprenticeship listing on berufsberatung.ch called?
73063.e: LENA stands for “Lehrstellennachweis”, the apprenticeship listing. Training companies post open apprenticeships there, which you can search by job and place.
73063.m: You find open apprenticeships in the LENA listing.

73064.q: What do you find on berufsberatung.ch for each job?
a: A description with tasks and requirements
The phone number of every apprentice
The marks of all final exams
73064.e: For each job there is information on tasks, requirements, training and further education options. Photos and films often add to the description.
73064.m: On berufsberatung.ch you find a description of every job.

73065.q: In which national languages is berufsberatung.ch available?
73065.e: The website exists in German, French (orientation.ch) and Italian (orientamento.ch). That way it reaches young people in all the major language regions.
73065.m: berufsberatung.ch is also available in French and Italian.

73066.q: What can you find out with an interest test for choosing a career?
a: Which mark you will get in your report
Whether you will definitely get the apprenticeship
73066.e: In an interest test you answer questions about activities you enjoy. Afterwards you get suggestions for suitable jobs that you can look at more closely.
73066.m: An interest test shows you jobs that match your interests.

73067.q: What is the most important task of careers advice?
a: To support young people in choosing their training
To hand out apprenticeships to young people
73067.e: Careers advisers support young people so that they find suitable training. But the young people make the decision themselves.
73067.m: Careers advice supports you, but you decide yourself.

73068.q: What does “choosing a career is a process” mean?
a: It happens in several steps over a longer time
It is done in a single day
It is decided by a court
It only happens after the apprenticeship
73068.e: Choosing a career includes steps such as getting to know yourself, exploring jobs, taster placements, deciding and applying. It usually takes more than a year.
73068.m: Choosing a career happens in several steps.

73069.q: Where are open apprenticeships often advertised?
a: Only on posters at the station
73069.e: Open apprenticeships are mainly found on online job boards such as LENA, on company websites and through personal contacts.
73069.m: You find many apprenticeships on online job boards.

73070.q: When looking for an apprenticeship, what is a “speculative” or “blind” application?
a: An application without an advertised vacancy
73070.e: With a speculative application you apply to a company that has not advertised an apprenticeship. Sometimes this still leads to a chance.
73070.m: You can send a speculative application even without an advertised vacancy.

73071.q: Why is a network of relatives and acquaintances helpful when looking for an apprenticeship?
a: They often know about open apprenticeships
They may sign the apprenticeship contract
They can improve your school marks
73071.e: Many apprenticeships are filled through contacts before they are advertised publicly. That is why it is worth telling people around you what you are looking for.
73071.m: Tell the people around you which apprenticeship you are looking for.

73072.q: What does an application plan or application list show?
a: When and where you applied and how things stand
Your marks for the last three years
The holidays at the training company
73072.e: If you send lots of applications, it is easy to lose track. A list with the date, company and reply helps you follow up.
73072.m: An application list gives you an overview of your applications.

73073.q: Who signs the apprenticeship contract if the apprentice is not yet 18?
a: The parents or legal guardian as well
73073.e: For under-18s, the legal representative, usually the parents, must also sign the apprenticeship contract. After that the canton approves it.
73073.m: For under-18s, the parents also sign the apprenticeship contract.

73074.q: What should you do if you have accepted an apprenticeship and still have other applications open?
a: Tell the other companies and withdraw
Just let all the applications carry on
73074.e: Once you have accepted an apprenticeship, you politely withdraw your other applications. That way the companies can give the place to other young people.
73074.m: After accepting an offer, you withdraw your other applications.

73075.q: What should you do if a training company takes a long time to reply to your application?
a: Politely ask by phone or email
Just turn up at the company and start working
Send exactly the same application again
73075.e: After about two weeks with no reply, you may ask in a friendly way. That shows interest and commitment.
73075.m: Asking politely shows the company your interest.

a: The collection of all your application documents
A folder with all your apprenticeship contracts
The list of all training companies
73076.e: The application file includes the cover letter, CV, copies of reports and other evidence. It is the applicant's calling card.
73076.m: Your application file is your calling card for the training company.

73077.q: Besides the cover letter and CV, what else often goes into an application file?
73077.e: Besides school reports, many companies want to see taster assessments and aptitude test results. They show performance and effort.
73077.m: Taster reports and test results complete your file.

73078.q: In what form do many companies want applications today?
a: As a PDF by email or through an online portal
As a handwritten letter on wrapping paper
As a photo on social media
73078.e: Many training companies accept applications digitally. So you should have all your documents ready as neat PDFs.
73078.m: Keep your application documents ready as neat PDF files.

73079.q: Why should you include copies of your school reports in your file rather than the originals?
a: Companies are not allowed to read originals
73079.e: Application documents are not always sent back. That is why you include copies and keep the originals.
73079.m: Always include copies of your reports.

73080.q: What is especially important about an application file?
a: Complete, neat and free of mistakes
As colourful as possible with lots of smileys
As long as possible, at least 30 pages
73080.e: A tidy file with no mistakes shows care. Spelling mistakes, on the other hand, leave a bad impression.
73080.m: A neat file with no mistakes shows that you take care.

73081.q: Which email address is best for an application?
a: One with your first name and surname
73081.e: A serious email address with your own name looks professional. Nicknames can look unprofessional.
73081.m: For applications, use a serious email address with your name.

73082.q: What is a reference in an application file?
a: A person who can give information about you
An encyclopedia to look things up in
73082.e: References are, for example, teachers or taster companies who may give the company information about you. You ask their permission first.
73082.m: Always ask your referees for their permission first.

73083.q: Why should you adapt your application file a little for each company?
a: Because every company and job has different requirements
Because identical files are not allowed
Because otherwise you get no holidays
73083.e: A file tailored to the company shows real interest. The cover letter in particular should be individual.
73083.m: Adapt your application for each company.

73084.q: What goes into a CV for an apprenticeship?
a: Personal details, schooling, taster placements and hobbies
The wage you want for every year
The names of all your classmates
73084.e: A CV gives an overview of who you are and what you have done. For young people it includes schools, taster placements, languages, hobbies and references.
73084.m: Your CV shows your path so far at a glance.

73085.q: How long should a CV for an apprenticeship usually be?
73085.e: A CV should be short and clear. For school leavers, one page is usually enough, two at most.
73085.m: A good CV is short and clear.

73086.q: What do you call a CV set out as a table?
73086.e: Today the tabular CV is the norm. The details are set out clearly in columns and sections.
73086.m: Today a CV is usually written as a table.

73087.q: What should a photo on your CV show?
a: A holiday picture on the beach
A group photo with your class
73087.e: A serious, recent portrait photo looks friendly and professional. Selfies or party pictures are not suitable.
73087.m: Use a recent, serious portrait photo on your CV.

73088.q: Why is it worth mentioning hobbies on your CV?
a: Because otherwise the CV is invalid
73088.e: Hobbies say something about your personality. Team sports, for example, show you can work in a team, and an instrument shows staying power.
73088.m: Hobbies on your CV say something about your personality.

73089.q: Which detail belongs to the personal details on a CV?
73089.e: Personal details include name, address, phone number, email and date of birth. Nationality is often given too.
73089.m: Your date of birth belongs in the personal details.

73090.q: In what order are schools usually listed on a tabular CV?
a: Most recent school first, or in clear time order
73090.e: What matters is a clear order in time that is easy to follow. Often the most recent stage is listed at the top.
73090.m: Put the stages of your CV in clear time order.

73091.q: What is a sensible way to give your language skills on a CV?
a: With the language and your level
With the names of your language teachers
Not at all, languages don't matter
73091.e: For languages you state which language you know and how well, such as native language, good knowledge or basic knowledge. That helps the company assess you.
73091.m: For each language, say how well you know it.

73092.q: What is the aim of a cover letter?
a: To explain why you want this particular apprenticeship
73092.e: In the cover letter you give reasons why you are interested in the job and the company. It should make them want to meet you.
73092.m: In your cover letter you show why you want the place.

73093.q: How long should a cover letter be?
73093.e: A cover letter is short and to the point. One A4 page is usually enough.
73093.m: A cover letter is about one page long.

73094.q: Which greeting is best in a cover letter?
73094.e: If you know the name of the person responsible, address them directly, for example “Dear Ms Muster”. That comes across as personal and polite.
73094.m: In your cover letter, address the person responsible by name.

73095.q: What should you avoid as far as possible in a cover letter?
a: General phrases that would fit any company
A mention of your taster placement
73095.e: Phrases like “I am motivated and a team player” without an example say little. Concrete experiences, for example from your taster placement, are better.
73095.m: Concrete examples are more convincing than empty phrases.

73096.q: What belongs at the end of a cover letter?
a: A request for an interview and a closing
A list of all your school marks
A joke to lighten the mood
73096.e: At the end you say thank you and express the wish to have an interview. Then come the closing and your signature.
73096.m: End your cover letter by asking for an interview.

73097.q: Why should you write something about the company in your cover letter?
a: It shows that you have found out about it
Because the company doesn't know itself
73097.e: If you mention what appeals to you about the company, you show real interest. You can find information on its website or during a taster placement.
73097.m: Find out about the company before you write.

73098.q: Who should read a cover letter before you send it?
a: A second person to check it
The training company, before you write it
73098.e: A second person often finds mistakes you overlook yourself. Parents, teachers or careers advisers are happy to help.
73098.m: Have your cover letter checked by someone else.

73099.q: What is a suitable closing at the end of a cover letter?
73099.e: In formal letters in Switzerland people usually write “Freundliche Grüsse” (kind regards). Casual phrases are out of place.
73099.m: A formal letter ends with “Kind regards”.

73100.q: What is especially important at a job interview?
a: Arriving on time and well prepared
73100.e: Being on time and prepared shows respect and interest. Find out about the company and the job beforehand.
73100.m: Arrive at the interview on time and well prepared.

73101.q: Which question is asked very often in a job interview?
a: Why do you want to learn this job?
What car do your parents drive?
How much pocket money do you get?
73101.e: Training companies want to know why you have chosen the job. A convincing answer with examples is important.
73101.m: Prepare an answer to why you want to learn the job.

73102.q: What do you do if you don't understand a question in the interview?
73102.e: Asking is allowed and shows you want to be precise. A wrong answer to a misunderstood question looks worse.
73102.m: If you don't understand something, ask politely.

73103.q: Why is it good to ask questions yourself at the end of the interview?
a: It shows interest in the company
Because otherwise you lose the apprenticeship
Because it makes the interview longer
73103.e: Your own questions, for example about how the apprenticeship works or what the tasks are, show real interest. You should prepare a few questions.
73103.m: Prepare your own questions for the interview.

73104.q: What should you do with your phone during a job interview?
a: Switch it off or put it on silent and put it away
Put it on the table and read messages
Leave the sound on for important calls
73104.e: A ringing phone or using it looks rude. It should be switched off in your bag during the interview.
73104.m: Switch your phone off before the interview.

73105.q: What clothing is suitable for a job interview?
a: Clean clothes that suit the job
73105.e: Your clothes should be neat and suit the job. In a workshop they are different from in a bank, but always tidy.
73105.m: Dress neatly and to suit the job.

73106.q: How can you prepare well for a job interview?
a: Play video games late the night before
Not at all, it's all about being spontaneous
Don't look at the company beforehand
73106.e: A role play with parents, a teacher or friends takes away nerves. You practise typical questions and introducing yourself.
73106.m: Practise the interview beforehand in a role play.

73107.q: How do you greet the interviewer at the start?
a: With eye contact, a friendly greeting and your name
Not at all, you just sit down
73107.e: A friendly greeting with eye contact makes a good first impression. You introduce yourself by name.
73107.m: First impressions count, so greet people warmly with eye contact.

73108.q: What is an aptitude test for when looking for an apprenticeship?
a: It checks whether you meet the requirements of a job
It replaces the final apprenticeship exam
73108.e: Aptitude tests check school knowledge and abilities such as logic or spatial awareness. Many companies use the results to choose candidates.
73108.m: An aptitude test shows whether you meet a job's requirements.

73109.q: Which aptitude test is widely used by training companies in German-speaking Switzerland?
73109.e: The Multicheck is a well-known aptitude test for young people looking for apprenticeships in Switzerland. There are different versions for different types of job.
73109.m: The Multicheck is a well-known aptitude test for apprenticeships.

73110.q: What is often tested in aptitude tests?
73110.e: Typical parts are arithmetic, German, foreign languages, logic and concentration. Depending on the type of job, other tasks are added.
73110.m: Aptitude tests often test maths, language and logic.

73111.q: How can you prepare for an aptitude test?
a: Stay awake as long as possible the day before
Not at all, preparing is forbidden
73111.e: With sample tasks you get to know the type of questions. That gives you confidence and saves time in the test.
73111.m: Sample tasks help you with the aptitude test.

73112.q: What does a spatial awareness task test?
a: Whether you can turn shapes and objects in your head
73112.e: Spatial awareness is important in technical jobs, such as draughtsman or mechanic. You have to turn shapes and put them together in your mind.
73112.m: Spatial thinking is especially important in technical jobs.

73113.q: Who usually pays for an aptitude test such as the Multicheck?
a: Often the young people or their parents
73113.e: Many aptitude tests charge a fee, which is usually paid by the young people or their parents. Some cantons or companies offer support.

73114.q: What should you do if an aptitude test went badly?
a: Retake it later or score points with other strengths
Give up choosing a career at once
73114.e: A test only shows part of your abilities. You can often retake it and win people over with good taster reports.
73114.m: A weak test is no reason to give up.

73115.q: Which ability does a concentration task test?
a: Whether you can work accurately for a long time
73115.e: In concentration tasks you have to find certain symbols quickly and without mistakes, for example. That shows how carefully you work.

73116.q: How should you react to a rejection?
a: Stay calm and learn from it
73116.e: Rejections are normal when looking for an apprenticeship. The important thing is not to give up and to improve your application if necessary.
73116.m: Rejections are part of looking for an apprenticeship.

73117.q: What can you politely ask the company after a rejection?
73117.e: Many companies give brief feedback if you ask politely. That way you find out what you can do better next time.
73117.m: After a rejection, politely ask for the reason.

73118.q: What makes particular sense after several rejections?
a: Checking your application documents with a careers adviser
Hoping for just one single place
73118.e: Careers advisers can check applications and give new ideas. A related job might also be a good fit.
73118.m: After rejections, have your application checked.

73119.q: Why is a “plan B” sensible when choosing a career?
a: You have an alternative if your dream job doesn't work out
Because a plan A is not allowed
Because the canton requires two apprenticeships
Because you do two apprenticeships at once
73119.e: Things don't always work out with your dream job. If you have a related job or a bridging solution ready, you don't lose time.
73119.m: A plan B gives you security when looking for an apprenticeship.

73120.q: What is a good way to deal with frustration after a rejection?
a: Take your anger out on others
73120.e: Talking to parents, friends or teachers helps you deal with disappointment. After that, the next step is easier.
73120.m: Talk about disappointments, then the next step is easier.

73121.q: What does a rejection show in most cases?
a: That another applicant was a better fit
That you will never find an apprenticeship
73121.e: Often lots of young people apply for the same place, and the company has to choose. So a rejection is not a judgement on you as a whole person.
73121.m: A rejection is not a judgement on your worth.

73122.q: What is the best way to respond to a written rejection?
a: Say thank you briefly and politely
With a complaint to the newspaper
With a new application the same day
73122.e: A short thank you leaves a good impression. A place might come up later, and the company will remember you.
73122.m: Say thank you politely even after a rejection.

a: An interim solution between school and apprenticeship
A holiday camp run by the municipality
73123.e: Bridging programmes help young people who have no apprenticeship yet after compulsory school. They prepare them for training.
73123.m: A bridging programme leads from school to an apprenticeship.

73124.q: Which option is a well-known interim solution after compulsory school?
73124.e: In the 10th school year you can fill gaps in your schooling and carry on looking for an apprenticeship. It usually lasts one year.
73124.m: The 10th school year is a well-known interim solution.

a: A year of practice at a company with school days, before the apprenticeship
The first week of the apprenticeship
The exam before the apprenticeship contract
73125.e: In a pre-apprenticeship you usually work three to four days at a company and go to school for one to two days. It prepares you for an apprenticeship.
73125.m: A pre-apprenticeship combines work at a company with school.

a: A programme for young people without an apprenticeship, with practice and application training
73126.e: The motivation semester is for young people with no next step lined up. It combines work placements, lessons and support with looking for an apprenticeship.
73126.m: SEMO supports young people in looking for an apprenticeship.

73127.q: Which interim solution combines working for a family with learning a language?
a: A stay as an au pair
73127.e: As an au pair you live with a host family, help in the home and with the children, and learn a language at the same time. Many go to French-speaking Switzerland or abroad for this.
73127.m: An au pair stay combines family work with learning a language.

73128.q: Why can an interim solution make sense?
a: You gain time and improve your chances
Because it leads to a university degree
Because you earn a high wage
73128.e: An interim solution gives you time to find your bearings and fill gaps. The important thing is to use it actively.
73128.m: An interim solution is a chance, not a defeat.

73129.q: What should you definitely keep doing during an interim solution?
73129.e: An interim solution is a bridge, not a goal. That is why the search for an apprenticeship carries on during it.
73129.m: Keep applying during an interim solution.

73130.q: Who does the integration pre-apprenticeship help to start an apprenticeship?
73130.e: The integration pre-apprenticeship prepares young refugees and young people who came to Switzerland late for an apprenticeship over one year. They also learn the language.
73130.m: The integration pre-apprenticeship prepares refugees for an apprenticeship.

73131.q: How long does basic vocational education with an EFZ last?
73131.e: An apprenticeship with a Federal VET Diploma (EFZ) lasts three or four years, depending on the job.
73131.m: An EFZ apprenticeship lasts three or four years.

73132.q: How long does basic vocational education with a Federal VET Certificate (EBA) last?
73132.e: The EBA programme lasts two years and is meant for young people with more practical strengths.
73132.m: An EBA apprenticeship lasts two years.

73133.q: What does the abbreviation EBA stand for?
73133.e: EBA means Eidgenössisches Berufsattest, the Federal VET Certificate. It is the qualification from the two-year programme.

73134.q: About how many jobs can young people in Switzerland choose from for an apprenticeship (as of 2025)?
73134.e: According to the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI), about 250 jobs are available to choose from.
73134.m: In Switzerland you can choose from about 250 apprenticeship jobs.

73135.q: What share of young people in Switzerland do an apprenticeship after compulsory school?
73135.e: According to SERI, about two thirds of young people choose basic vocational education with an EFZ or EBA.
73135.m: About two thirds of young people do an apprenticeship.

73136.q: What is the person at the training company who is responsible for training the apprentices called?
73136.e: At the company, an apprentice trainer supports the apprentices. This requires a special course for trainers.
73136.m: At the training company, an apprentice trainer trains the apprentices.

73137.q: What is set out in the same way across all of Switzerland for every apprenticeship?
a: What you learn and how long the apprenticeship lasts
Which town you have to live in
73137.e: For each job, the federal government sets out in a regulation how long the apprenticeship lasts, what you learn and what the exam is like. The wage is agreed between the company and the apprentice in the contract.
73137.m: Every apprenticeship has the same rules throughout Switzerland.

73138.q: Who regulates apprenticeships in Switzerland with its own law?
73138.e: The Federal Act on Vocational and Professional Education and Training applies throughout Switzerland. The cantons put it into practice.
73138.m: Apprenticeships are regulated by a federal law.

73139.q: Which qualification do you get after passing a three-year apprenticeship as a cook?
73139.e: Three- and four-year apprenticeships end with the Federal VET Diploma (EFZ). The EBA only exists after two-year programmes.
73139.m: After a three- or four-year apprenticeship you get an EFZ.

73140.q: Who must the training company inform immediately if an apprenticeship contract is ended early?
73140.e: According to the Vocational Training Act (Article 14), an early termination must be reported to the cantonal authority without delay.
73140.m: An ended apprenticeship must be reported to the canton.

73141.q: In which month do most apprenticeships in Switzerland start?
73141.e: Most apprenticeships start in summer, usually in August, together with the new school year at the vocational school.

73142.q: Which office must approve an apprenticeship contract?
73142.e: The training company submits the contract to the canton. The cantonal vocational training office checks and approves it.
73142.m: The canton approves every apprenticeship contract.

73143.q: What is the probation period at the start of an apprenticeship for?
a: Both sides check whether it works
You don't have to work yet
73143.e: During the probation period, the apprentice and the company find out whether the job and working together suit them. It usually lasts three months.
73143.m: In the probation period both sides check whether it works.

73144.q: Can the probation period of an apprenticeship be extended?
a: Yes, in exceptional cases with the canton's approval
Yes, for as long as you like
73144.e: If necessary, the probation period can be extended with the canton's approval, to a maximum of six months.
73144.m: The probation period can be extended in exceptional cases.

73145.q: What applies if notice is given during the probation period of an apprenticeship?
a: You can leave at short notice
You cannot give notice at all
You have to wait a year
Only the company may give notice
73145.e: During the probation period, both sides can give notice with a short period of seven days. Later, there must be important reasons.
73145.m: During the probation period, giving notice is easy.

73146.q: When may an apprenticeship contract be ended early after the probation period?
a: At any time without a reason
Never, not even in an emergency
73146.e: After the probation period, ending it without notice is only possible for important reasons, for example if the company can no longer provide training.
73146.m: After the probation period, you need important reasons to end an apprenticeship.

73147.q: Among other things, what must be written in the apprenticeship contract?
73147.e: The apprenticeship contract sets out at least the type and length of training, wages, probation period, working hours and holidays.
73147.m: The apprenticeship contract states wages, working hours and holidays.

73148.q: Who makes an apprenticeship contract with each other?
a: The training company and the apprentice
The parents and the vocational school
The federal government and the municipality
73148.e: The parties to the contract are the training company and the apprentice. The canton only approves the contract.
73148.m: The training company and the apprentice make the apprenticeship contract.

73149.q: About how many days a week do apprentices go to vocational school?
73149.e: Apprentices usually go to school one or two days a week. The rest of the time they work at the training company.
73149.m: Apprentices spend about one to two days a week at vocational school.

73150.q: What do compulsory lessons at vocational school cost apprentices?
73150.e: According to the Vocational Training Act (Article 22), compulsory lessons at vocational schools are free of charge.
73150.m: Compulsory lessons at vocational school are free.

73151.q: What do you learn in general education lessons at vocational school?
a: Topics such as law, politics and language
Only the theory of your own job
73151.e: General education lessons (ABU) cover topics from society, law, politics, the economy and language. You learn the theory of your job in vocational subject lessons.
73151.m: In ABU you learn things you need for everyday life and society.

73152.q: Besides vocational subjects and general education, which subject is compulsory at vocational school?
73152.e: In Switzerland, sport lessons are also required in basic vocational education.
73152.m: Vocational school also has compulsory sport lessons.

73153.q: Do lessons at vocational school count as working time for apprentices?
a: Yes, with no deduction from wages
73153.e: The training company must give apprentices time off for compulsory lessons, with no deduction from their wages (Article 345a of the Code of Obligations).
73153.m: School time counts as working time for apprentices.

73154.q: What does the vocational school offer apprentices who have learning difficulties?
73154.e: Vocational schools offer support courses for apprentices who are struggling and optional courses for those who are especially interested.
73154.m: If you struggle, you can take support courses at vocational school.

73155.q: What do apprentices learn in vocational subject lessons at vocational school?
a: The theoretical knowledge of their job
73155.e: In vocational subject lessons, apprentices learn the theory of their job, for example materials or job-related maths.
73155.m: In vocational subject lessons you learn the theory of your own job.

73156.q: What are the courses called that apprentices with good results can also choose at vocational school?
73156.e: Optional courses are voluntary extras, such as languages. The company must allow them with no deduction from wages, as long as the apprentice's results are good.
73156.m: Optional courses are voluntary extra courses at vocational school.

73157.q: Who pays the costs of the inter-company courses?
73157.e: According to the Vocational Training Ordinance, the training company bears the costs. The course costs may not be passed on to apprentices.
73157.m: The training company pays for inter-company courses, not the apprentices.

73158.q: Is attending the inter-company courses voluntary for apprentices?
73158.e: Attending the üK is compulsory for apprentices if the training regulations for the job provide for such courses.

73159.q: Who usually organises the inter-company courses?
73159.e: The professional associations, known as organisations of the world of work (OdA), are usually responsible.
73159.m: Inter-company courses are usually organised by the professional associations.

73160.q: Together with the federal government and the cantons, who decides what is learned in an apprenticeship?
73160.e: The professional associations, also called organisations of the world of work (OdA), know their trade best. That is why they help decide what an apprenticeship covers.
73160.m: The professional associations help decide what an apprenticeship covers.

73161.q: How many places of learning does basic vocational education in Switzerland have?
73161.e: The three places of learning are the training company, the vocational school and the inter-company courses.
73161.m: An apprenticeship takes place at three places of learning.

73162.q: Where do the inter-company courses (üK) usually take place?
a: At a professional association's training centre
