They doubled the imputed rental value
73902.e: On 28 September 2025, the people and the cantons accepted the proposal that clears the way to abolishing the imputed rental value on owner-occupied homes. In return, many tax deductions disappear.
73902.m: With the 2025 vote, the change of system for the imputed rental value was decided.

73903.q: How much equity do banks usually require at least for buying a home?
a: 20 per cent of the purchase price
5 per cent of the purchase price
50 per cent of the purchase price
73903.e: Banks usually finance at most 80 per cent of the purchase price with a mortgage. At least 10 per cent must come from your own funds outside the pension fund.
73903.m: Anyone who wants to buy a house needs at least a fifth in equity.

73904.q: What does “assisted living” mean for older people?
a: Your own flat with support and emergency services
73904.e: In assisted living, older people live independently in their own flat. When needed, services such as an emergency call, cleaning or care are available.
73904.m: Assisted living combines independence with safety.

73905.q: What is the legal maximum interest rate for cash loans in Switzerland (as of 2026)?
73905.e: Since 1 January 2026 the Consumer Credit Ordinance has limited the interest on cash loans to 10 per cent; in 2025 it was still 11 per cent. For overdraft credit such as credit cards with a credit option, the limit is 12 per cent.
73905.m: Cash loans in Switzerland may cost at most 10 per cent interest.

73906.q: Within what time limit can you withdraw from a consumer credit agreement?
73906.e: Under Art. 16 of the Consumer Credit Act, the consumer can withdraw from the agreement in writing within 14 days. This way the law protects against hasty decisions.
73906.m: You can withdraw from a consumer loan within 14 days.

73907.q: What must the lender check before giving a cash loan?
a: Whether the loan can be repaid within 36 months without touching the minimum needed to live
Whether the customer owns a car
Whether the customer belongs to a club
Whether the customer has ever moved house
73907.e: The Consumer Credit Act requires a creditworthiness check: the loan must be repayable within 36 months without using the part of income that cannot be seized (Art. 28 of the Consumer Credit Act).
73907.m: A loan may only be given if it can be repaid affordably.

73908.q: Which body in Switzerland collects data on current consumer loans so that lenders can check people's debts?
73908.e: Lenders must report consumer loans to the IKO. That way other lenders can see whether a person already has loans or leasing contracts.
73908.m: The IKO helps prevent over-indebtedness from too many loans.

73909.q: Which type of contract also falls under the Consumer Credit Act?
a: The tenancy agreement for a flat
73909.e: Leasing contracts for consumer goods, such as car leasing, count as consumer credit. The creditworthiness check and the right of withdrawal apply here too.
73909.m: Leasing is legally a form of consumer credit.

73910.q: Roughly how much interest do you pay in one year on a loan of 5,000 francs at 10 per cent a year, if nothing has been repaid yet?
73910.e: 10 per cent of 5,000 francs is 5,000 times 0.1, which equals 500 francs. If you repay in instalments, the interest on the falling remaining debt is a bit lower.
73910.m: A consumer loan costs a lot of interest and makes every purchase more expensive.

73911.q: Which kind of advertising for consumer loans is banned in Switzerland?
a: Advertising that states the interest rate
73911.e: Since 2016 the Unfair Competition Act has banned aggressive advertising for consumer loans. The industry has also set its own rules, which rule out, for example, advertising aimed at young people.
73911.m: In Switzerland loans may not be advertised aggressively.

73912.q: Which document does a debtor receive as the first step of debt collection proceedings?
73912.e: After the creditor's request for debt collection, the debt collection office serves the debtor with a payment order. It asks him to pay the debt within 20 days.
73912.m: Debt collection begins with the payment order.

73913.q: Within what time limit after it is served can a debtor raise an objection in debt collection proceedings?
73913.e: Under Art. 74 of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, the objection must be raised within 10 days of the order being served. It stops the debt collection for the time being.
73913.m: Anyone who disputes a claim raises an objection within 10 days.

73914.q: When starting debt collection proceedings, must a creditor prove that their claim exists?
a: No, the debt collection office does not check the claim
73914.e: In Switzerland anyone can start debt collection proceedings without proving the claim. Only after an objection must the creditor prove their claim.
73914.m: Debt collection can be started without proof, which is why the objection matters.

73915.q: What must a creditor do if the debtor has raised an objection and the debt collection is to continue?
a: Have the objection set aside by a court
Simply send a second payment order
Send the police to the debtor
Nothing, the debt collection continues automatically
73915.e: The objection stops the debt collection. The creditor must show in court that the claim exists, for example with a signed acknowledgement of debt.
73915.m: After an objection, the creditor needs a court decision.

73916.q: What does a debtor always keep when their wages are seized?
a: The minimum subsistence level under debt collection law
73916.e: Only the part of income above the minimum subsistence level may be seized (Art. 93 of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act). What is absolutely needed to live stays with the debtor.
73916.m: In a seizure, the minimum subsistence level stays protected.

73917.q: When does a claim backed by a certificate of unpaid debt expire?
73917.e: Under Art. 149a of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, claims from a certificate of unpaid debt expire 20 years after the certificate is issued. Until then the creditor can start debt collection again.
73917.m: A certificate of unpaid debt can follow a debtor for decades.

73918.q: For how long after proceedings have ended may third parties still see debt collection entries in the register?
73918.e: Under Art. 8a of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, third parties no longer receive information about proceedings five years after they have ended. That is why a debt collection entry can make flat hunting harder for years.
73918.m: Debt collection entries stay visible to third parties for five years.

73919.q: Since 2019, what can a person do against unjustified debt collection so that it is not disclosed to third parties?
a: Apply for non-disclosure, at the earliest after three months
73919.e: Under Art. 8a para. 3 let. d of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, the debtor can apply at the earliest three months after the debt collection began. If the creditor does not show within 20 days that he has started proceedings to set aside the objection, the debt collection is no longer disclosed to third parties.
73919.m: Against unjustified debt collection there is the application for non-disclosure.

73920.q: At which debt collection office are proceedings against a private person usually started?
a: At the debtor's place of residence
At the creditor's place of residence
At the debtor's place of birth
73920.e: Under Art. 46 of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, the debtor is pursued at their place of residence. If the debtor moves, the office at the new place of residence is responsible.
73920.m: Debt collection happens where you live.

73921.q: You knocked over the vase by accident. What is the honest thing to do?
73921.e: Being honest means telling the truth, even when you have made a mistake. Accidents can happen to anyone.
73921.m: Owning up to a mistake is honest.

73922.q: What is it called when someone says something untrue on purpose?
73922.e: A lie is something you say that you know is not true. You want to trick others with it.
73922.m: A lie is untrue on purpose.

73923.q: You find someone else's purse in the playground. What do you do?
73923.e: Things you find belong to someone else. If you hand them in, you help the owner get them back.

73924.q: Why is honesty important for friends?
73924.e: When friends are honest, they know they can believe each other. That is how trust grows.

73925.q: Your friend cheated in a game and you saw it. What is fair and honest?
73925.e: If you calmly mention the cheating, you stay honest and fair. Laughing or cheating yourself makes it worse.
73925.m: Calmly speak up about things that are unfair.

73926.q: What often happens when you tell one lie?
73926.e: One lie often leads to more lies so that it isn't found out. That quickly becomes tiring.
73926.m: One lie often leads to more lies.

73927.q: Which sentence is honest if you forgot your homework?
73927.e: Only the first sentence says what really happened. The other sentences are not true.
73927.m: Honest means saying what really happened.

a: A reason that isn't quite true
73928.e: With an excuse, you try to talk your way out of something. The reason you give is often not true.
73928.m: An excuse distracts from the truth.

73929.q: What makes someone a good friend?
73929.e: Good friends support each other, even when things are difficult. They are there for each other.

73930.q: Your friend is sad. What can you do?
73930.e: Asking shows that the other person matters to you. Often just listening helps.

73931.q: A new child is in the class and doesn't know anyone. What is kind?
a: Copy them to make fun of them
73931.e: New children often feel unsure. An invitation to play helps them fit in.
73931.m: New children are happy to be invited.

73932.q: Can you be friends with more than one child?
a: No, only with children from your own class
No, only with your own brothers and sisters
73932.e: You can have lots of friends. Every friendship is something special.
73932.m: You can have lots of friends.

73933.q: Your friend tells you a secret that doesn't harm anyone. What do you do?
a: Write it down and hand it out
73933.e: Keeping a secret shows that you can be trusted. Then your friend can tell you things later on too.

73934.q: Which kind of secret should you tell an adult you trust?
73934.e: Secrets where someone is afraid or being hurt can and should be told to someone you trust. That is not betrayal.

73935.q: How do you show a friend that you like them?
73935.e: Spending time together shows that someone matters to you. Playing, talking and laughing make a friendship stronger.

73936.q: Your friend made a mistake while drawing and is sad. What do you say?
73936.e: Encouraging words comfort your friend and show that you are on her side. Everyone makes mistakes.
73936.m: Good friends cheer each other up.

73937.e: A compliment is a friendly remark, for example “You've drawn that really well”. It makes others happy.

73938.q: You have three apples and your friend has none. What is kind?
73938.e: When you share, you think of others too. Then you both have something.

73939.q: You share 8 jelly sweets fairly with a friend. How many does each of you get?
73939.e: 8 divided by 2 is 4. That way you each have the same number.
73939.m: When you share fairly, everyone gets the same amount.

73940.q: Two children want the same swing. What is a good solution?
73940.e: Taking turns is a way of sharing. Everyone gets a go.

73941.q: Apart from things, what else can you share?
73941.e: You can also share time, ideas and joy with others. That costs nothing.
73941.m: You can share time and joy too.

73942.q: Can you just take something that belongs to someone else to share it?
a: Yes, if the owner is away
73942.e: Sharing something that isn't yours is only OK with permission. Otherwise you are taking something away from someone.
73942.m: Only share other people's things with permission.

73943.q: You cut a pizza into 4 equal pieces for 4 children. How many pieces does each child get?
73943.e: 4 pieces for 4 children is 1 piece per child. That is fair.
73943.m: The same number of pieces is fair.

73944.q: How do you politely ask if you can borrow something?
73944.e: Saying “please” is asking politely. Then the other person can decide for themselves.

73945.q: What do you do with a borrowed book?
73945.e: Borrowed things belong to someone else. You look after them well and give them back.

73946.q: In a race, one child starts too early. Is that fair?
a: No, everyone should start at the same time
Yes, fast people can start earlier
Yes, if they really want to win
73946.e: Starting too early gives you an unfair advantage. Everyone should start running at the same time.
73946.m: In a fair race, everyone starts at the same time.

73947.q: How does a fair winner behave?
73947.e: If you win and stay friendly, you don't hurt anyone. Laughing at others spoils the fun for everyone.

73948.q: What is fair behaviour in sport called?
73948.e: Fair play means keeping to the rules and respecting your opponent.

73949.q: How can you fairly decide who starts in a game?
73949.e: When you roll a dice, every child has the same chance. That is fair.
73949.m: Rolling a dice gives everyone the same chance.

73950.q: A child can't run because of a plaster cast. What is fair in the game?
73950.e: Being fair sometimes means being considerate. With a suitable job, the child can still join in.
73950.m: Fair is when everyone can join in.

73951.q: What is a foul in football?
73951.e: A foul is breaking the rules of the game, for example tripping someone up. There is a penalty for it.
73951.m: A foul is against the rules.

73952.q: A child has fallen over and is crying. What do you do?
73952.e: Helpful people look after others when they need help. If someone is hurt, you fetch an adult.
73952.m: Someone who falls over needs help.

73953.q: Who do you call on 144 in Switzerland after a bad accident?
73953.e: In Switzerland, 144 is the emergency number for the ambulance service, the rescue service with the ambulance.
73953.m: You reach the ambulance service on 144.

73954.q: What is the emergency number for the fire brigade in Switzerland?
73954.e: In Switzerland you reach the fire brigade on 118. You call them, for example, if there is a fire.

73955.q: Which number can children in Switzerland call when they are worried?
73955.e: The number 147 from Pro Juventute is there for children and young people. Someone listens and helps there, day and night and free of charge.
73955.m: When you're worried, the number 147 helps.

73956.q: An older man is carrying heavy bags up the stairs. What is helpful?
73956.e: If you first ask whether help is wanted, you are helpful and polite. The other person can then say yes or no.
73956.m: Offer help in a friendly way.

73957.q: How can you help at home?
73957.e: Small jobs like laying the table help the whole family. Then one person doesn't have to do everything alone.

73958.q: What do you say when someone has helped you?
73958.e: Saying “thank you” shows that you value the help. That makes the helper happy.

73959.q: How does a child who is laughing and jumping feel?
73959.e: Laughing and jumping are typical signs of joy.
73959.m: Someone who laughs is often happy.

73960.q: A child has tears in their eyes and their head is hanging down. How do they probably feel?
73960.e: Tears and a hanging head often show sadness. You can ask what is wrong.

73961.q: A child is clenching their fists and has a red face. What feeling do they probably have?
73961.e: Clenched fists and a red face are often signs of anger. You can ask the child what is wrong.

73962.q: What can help when you are very angry?
73962.e: Breathing deeply calms the body. Afterwards you can say better what is bothering you.
73962.m: Deep breaths calm you down when you're angry.

73963.q: What is the feeling called when you are frightened of something?
73963.e: Fear warns us about dangers. It is good to talk to someone about it.

73964.q: You have finished painting a difficult picture. Which feeling fits?
73964.e: When you have managed something difficult, you are proud of it.
73964.m: When you've managed something, you're proud.

73965.q: What is it called when you can feel what others are feeling?
73965.e: Empathy means you sense how someone else is feeling. Then you can help better.

73966.q: What is the feeling called when you want something that someone else has?
73966.e: You feel envy when you begrudge someone something or want it yourself. Everyone has this feeling sometimes.

73967.e: All feelings are allowed, including anger and sadness. What matters is how you deal with them.

73968.q: What helps most when two children are arguing?
73968.e: When you talk to each other, you understand what is bothering the other person. That way you find a solution.

73969.q: How do you start a sentence to say what bothers you without blaming someone?
73969.e: An “I” sentence says how you feel without attacking the other person. That way the other person listens better.

73970.q: What should you do while the other person explains in an argument?
73970.e: If you listen, you find out why the other person is upset. Then it's your turn.

73971.q: What is a solution called where both sides give in a little?
73971.e: In a compromise, everyone gets some of what they want. So in the end both are fairly happy.
73971.m: In a compromise, both give in.

73972.q: Who can help if children can't sort out their argument on their own?
73972.e: Teachers or parents can help find a solution. In some schools, trained children also help as “peacemakers”.
73972.m: In a difficult argument, get help.

73973.q: What is not a good idea in an argument?
73973.e: Violence hurts and makes the argument worse. Talking, listening or taking a break help.

73974.q: Why can a short break help in an argument?
73974.e: With a bit of distance, you get calmer. Afterwards you usually talk to each other in a friendlier way.
73974.m: A break helps everyone calm down.

73975.q: What is a person called who helps two people who are arguing to sort things out?
73975.e: A mediator helps both sides listen to each other and find a solution. They don't take sides.

73976.q: Two children want to read the same book. Which solution is peaceful?
73976.e: If both read together, both get something out of it. That way there is no argument.

73977.q: You bumped into someone by accident. What do you say?
73977.e: You say sorry even if it was an accident. That way the other person knows it wasn't on purpose.

73978.q: What is part of a good apology?
73978.e: If you apologise properly, you say what you did wrong. That shows you are sorry.

73979.q: Apart from words, how can you show you are sorry?
73979.e: If, for example, you build a tower back up after knocking it over, you put the damage right. That shows you mean it.
73979.m: Putting things right shows you are sorry.

73980.q: Someone apologises to you. What can you answer?
73980.e: Accepting an apology ends the argument. Afterwards you can play together again.

73981.q: What is it called when you no longer hold a mistake against someone?
73981.e: Forgiving means letting go of being angry. That does both people good.
73981.m: Forgiving means letting go of anger.

73982.q: What would be a bad apology?
73982.e: If you blame the other person in the same sentence, you aren't really apologising. A real apology has no “but”.

73983.q: What is it called when two people become friends again after an argument?
73983.e: When two people make up, they put their argument behind them. It often starts with an apology.
73983.m: After the argument comes making up.

73984.q: When is the best time to apologise?
a: Only when the other person asks for it
73984.e: The sooner you apologise, the sooner the anger is over.

73985.e: If you let others finish speaking, you show that their opinion matters. That is respectful.
73985.m: Letting people finish speaking is respectful.

73986.q: What do people in German-speaking Switzerland often say as a greeting?
73986.e: “Grüezi” is a common, polite greeting in German-speaking Switzerland. Greeting people shows respect.

73987.q: How do you treat other people's things respectfully?
73987.e: Other people's things belong to someone else. You handle them carefully.
